intended_object: Local representation of quadratic forms over a number field K: Q is represented by R over every completion K_v, i.e. for every place v there is an injective K_v-linear isometry Q⊗K_v → R⊗K_v. This is the hypothesis of the Hasse–Minkowski local–global principle for representations. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the name.
explanation:
The body requires `IsRepresentedBy` at every finite place and at every real place. Here `IsRepresentedBy` means there is an injective isometry `Q →qᵢ R`, which is the standard notion of one form representing another. `atFinitePlace` is the base change of the form to the adic completion `v.adicCompletion K`, ranging over all height-one primes of 𝓞 K. `atRealPlace` is the base change to ℝ along the real embedding. So the definition requires a local representation at every non-archimedean place and at every real place.

Complex places are left out, and the module documentation says so explicitly. This is harmless. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, whether one form represents another depends only on the dimensions and ranks of the forms, and these do not change under field extension. A representation over K_v therefore gives one over an algebraic closure of K_v, and hence over ℂ. Since every number field has finite places, the complex condition follows from the finite-place conditions. The definition is therefore equivalent to requiring representation at all places.

The definition is stated for number fields, which is the standard setting for this local–global notion, and the construction uses the specific structure of number-field places (the adic completions and the real embeddings). One could extend it to all global fields, but number fields are the usual setting and are not artificially narrow. Mathlib has no notion of local representation of quadratic forms.
